Using the autoprotolysis constants of 2-(4-trifluoromethanesulfonato)phenylmalononitrile as an anchor, the p K a values of eight organophosphonium bistriflimides are experimentally determined in three polar fluorinated arenes via 31 P{ 1 H} NMR spectroscopic titration. Subsequently, the p K a values of eight corresponding organophosphonium tetrafluoroborates and eight corresponding organophosphonium tetraphenylborates soluble in o -difluorobenzene are further experimentally determined.

title: Hydrogen Pretreatment Programs Oxidative Surface Reconstruction for Enhanced Lattice-Oxygen Reactivity in Co3O4
abstract: The oxidation activity of reducible oxides is closely linked to the nature of lattice oxygen species, and reductive treatments are often used to tailor the low-temperature reactivity by modifying the surface coordination environment. Here, using Co3O4 and the oxidation of 2-propanol as a model reaction, we demonstrate that a further enhancement of the low-temperature activity can be achieved by extending the reduction beyond conventional surface modification to access distinct, metastable CoO surface terminations.

title: Selective Mono and Diborylation of Aromatic Pentafluorosulfanyl Compounds by iridium-catalyzed C–H Activation
Iridium Oxidation-State Dynamics during Transient Operation under PEM Water Electrolysis Single-Cell Conditions Revealed by Time-Resolved Operando XAS
abstract: Resolving the oxidation-state dynamics of Ir oxide anode catalysts during individual potential transients in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) single cells remains challenging. Here, we developed an operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) cell based on a modified lab-scale single-cell design and performed super quick XAS (SQXAS) measurements with a time resolution of ca. 200 ms.

title: Remote C(sp3)–H Functionalization via Visible-Light-Mediated Generation of Amidyl Radicals from Readily Accessible Arylsulfonamides
abstract: Remote C(sp3)–H functionalization via amidyl radical-mediated 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis and late-stage modification of structurally complex molecules. However, practical methods for amidyl radical generation that combine easily prepared precursors with mild reaction conditions remain highly desirable. Herein, we report a visible-light-mediated method for generating amidyl radicals from readily accessible arylsulfonamides through precise tuning of the reduction potential of the arylsulfonyl group.

title: ChiroptMap: Orbital-Cube-Free Transition-Moment Density Maps from Gaussian and ORCA
abstract: Earlier cube-based workflows generated electric-and magnetic-dipole transition-moment maps from molecular-orbital cubes exported with Gaussian cubegen from formatted-checkpoint data. ChiroptMap instead evaluates canonical orbitals and analytical derivatives blockwise from Gaussian WFX or an ORCA output/JSON/WFX bridge, eliminating intermediate orbital cubes while retaining final visualization cubes and S1–S6 CPL CSV values.

title: Computationally Guided Discovery of Cannabinoid Derivatives for Antiviral and Anticancer Applications: From Chemical Space to Experimental Validation
abstract: Cannabinoids represent a chemically diverse and structurally tunable class of natural and synthetic compounds that have attracted growing interest as molecular scaffolds for therapeutic discovery. However, their extensive chemical diversity, polypharmacology, conformational flexibility, and complex pharmacokinetic properties make the systematic identification and optimisation of therapeutically useful derivatives challenging.

title: Ge–N Cooperativity and Catalytic Hydrodefluorination by a Pyridine Dipyrrolide Germanium Platform
abstract: p-Block elements are emerging as sustainable alternatives to transition metals in catalysis, but the development of new species capable of redox cycling poses a central challenge to achieving metallomimetic reactivity. Redox-neutral processes offer a powerful strategy to circumvent challenging reductive elimination steps. Despite promising early applications of germanium(II)–ligand cooperativity for stoichiometric bond activation, the use of germylenes in redox-neutral catalysis remains largely limited to hydrofunctionalization of polar unsaturated bonds.

title: Molecular Engineering of a Small-Molecular Yellow-to-Orange Carbonyl-based Multi-Resonance TADF Emitter
abstract: Red-shifting MR-TADF emitters via donor substitution is an established strategy; however, this typically results in broadened emission and reduced photoluminescence quantum yields (FPL). We report tBuInPZ-DiKTa, fusing an indolophenazine donor directly to the DiKTa core, achieving an unprecedented red-shift for fused DiKTa-based emitters while preserving narrowband emission and high FPL.

title: Expanding the Cygnet Class of Solvents: Development of a Series of Bio-based Polar Aprotic High Boiling Solvents
abstract: Polar aprotic solvents have many applications in organic chemistry, but there are few bio-based substitutes available. As legislation becomes more restrictive due to health and safety concerns, the need for safer and more sustainable solvents has become ever more pressing. Here, we have built on previous works to synthesise several derivatives of the cellulose-derived Cyrene through an environmentally friendly ketalisation reaction, resulting in a class of solvents called the Cygnets.

title: Colloidal Interactions in Low-polarity Dispersions of Permanently Magnetic Nanoplatelets
abstract: Ferrofluids based on permanently magnetic nanoplatelets are attractive functional materials. However, their preparation in low-polarity media is particularly challenging because magnetic dipole–dipole interactions strongly promote agglomeration while conventional electrostatic stabilisation is weakened. Here, low-polarity dispersions of barium hexaferrite nanoplatelets were prepared by functionalising the particles with ricinoleic acid (RA) and dispersing them in low-polarity solvents of different chemical character.

title: Correlative super-resolution microscopy reveals preferential localization of quantum color center formation on carbon nanotubes
abstract: Covalent quantum color centers, (CCs) introduced onto single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) create localized, red-shifted emission states with promising applications in quantum photonics, biosensing and bioimaging. Yet, the mechanisms governing where and how these color centers form on the SWCNTs remain poorly understood. title: Excitation-Dependent Spin-State Relaxation Mediated by Jahn–Teller Motion in a Mn(III) Complex
abstract: Photoexcited transition-metal complexes exhibit complex excited-state dynamics arising from the interplay of electronic relaxation, spin-state conversion, and nuclear motion. Here, we use quantum dynamics to investigate the ultrafast photodynamics of the Jahn–Teller active complex Mn(terpy)Cl3. The high-spin d4 electronic configuration of Mn(III) produces strong coupling between electronic structure and molecular geometry, making this system an ideal platform for exploring nonadiabatic relaxation and spin-state evolution.

title: Supramolecular Polymers of Chiral and Achiral Rhodium and Iridium Complexes of N-confused Porphyrin
abstract: A series of rhodium(III) and iridium(III) complexes of N-confused porphyrin (NCP) was synthesized and characterized by spectroscopic, electrochemical, and XRD methods. The results were analyzed and corroborated by DFT calculations. Insertion of the metal ions was carried out in the presence of primary alcohols (EtOH, n-PrOH), affording diamagnetic chiral square-pyramidal complexes, HNCPM(Acyl), bearing a C-bonded apical acyl ligand.

title: Vertical quantum confinement in bulk MoS$_2$
abstract: We experimentally observe quantum confinement states in bulk MoS$_2$ using Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES). The band structure at the $\overlineΓ$ point reveals quantum well states (QWSs) linked to vertical quantum confinement of the electrons, confirmed by the absence of dispersion in k$_z$ and a strong intensity modulation with photon energy. Notably, the binding energy dependence of the QWSs vs $n$ does not follow the quadratic dependence of a two-dimensional electron gas. Instead, a linear behaviour is observed that is consistent with a parabolic-like quantum well. This confinement arises from the mechanical exfoliation preparation method, which leads to the detachment of a multilayer stack from the underlying bulk. This is confirmed by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. The quantum confinement in bulk-like MoS$_2$ not only offers the opportunity to explore intersubband transitions to exploit optical properties but also provides a means to study fundamental quantum phenomena in multilayer stacks of different thicknesses.

title: Regulating Zn2+ Desolvation and (002)-Oriented Deposition for Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
abstract: Dendrite growth and interfacial side reactions of zinc metal anodes severely constrain the practical application of aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Here, a simple and well-established strategy is proposed by constructing a polyimide/UiO-66-NH2 composite interlayer (Zn@PI-UiO-66-NH2) with a three-dimensional porous structure on the surface of zinc foil via electrospinning followed by thermal imidization.

title: Contact Electrification of Individual Water Microdroplets Inside Mass Spectrometers Leads to Extensive Oxidation or Reduction Irrespective of Initial Droplet Charge or Polarity
abstract: Charged water microdroplets that are aerodynamically accelerated upon introduction into an atmospheric sampling mass spectrometer interface can undergo glancing collisions that lead to surprising electrochemical processes. A custom charge detection instrument with a 24-element detector array is used to determine the outcomes of glancing collisions of individual charged water microdroplets with stainless-steel surfaces over a well-defined and narrow angle of ∼0.15° ± 0.03°. Water droplets entering the high-vacuum region with angles of <0.11° pass through the detector unimpeded and have kinetic energies in the MeV range depending on droplet size due to aerodynamic acceleration alone. Droplets that have glancing surface collisions undergo extensive oxidation or reduction through the removal or addition of up to tens of thousands of electrons per collision, independent of their initial charge or polarity, although some ion transfer may also play a role. The propensity for these two electrochemical processes appears stochastic, although more highly charged droplets appear to undergo charge reduction more readily. These results clearly demonstrate that highly energetic electrochemical processes of any type can occur within charged or uncharged aqueous microdroplets of any polarity that are introduced into mass spectrometers and may explain the observation of some unusual ions that have been reported in some microdroplet reaction studies.

title: Boosting Industrial Hydrogen Evolution via OH– Spillover on Ru Single Atoms Enabled by a Hierarchical Ni@Ni3C Core–Shell Architecture
abstract: Developing industrial-grade alkaline hydrogen evolution catalysts remains a critical challenge due to sluggish water dissociation and limited proton availability at the electrode–electrolyte interface. Here, we construct a metastable Ni/Ni3C core–shell structure and anchor atomically dispersed Ru single-atom sites (Ru SAs/Ni@Ni3C) to overcome this bottleneck. In situ studies reveal that Ru sites selectively adsorb hydroxyl species, enabling a dynamic OH– spillover that rapidly refreshes adjacent Ni active sites.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
